#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Average Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Average Analysis</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Average Analysis">

Displays a weighted average of meter analysis data for a selected time frame, calculated by product or total fluid.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Raw Data Count at the top right corner of the report indicates the number of final form daily records that were retrieved as the basis of average calculation according to the selected meter or location, time frame, and product. This report is available as a standard report for FLOWCAL 8.10.50.4 and 8.11.35, or above.

For component mole %, mass %, and liquid volume % average calculation, if a field is null for one or more records, but not all records, the value for the record is considered to be 0, not null. However, if a field is null for all records used for calculation, the average is null and is displayed as blank.

> <div class="example">
>
> <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" style="color: #525f39;" data-mc-targets="Example-Average Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>
>
> <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Average Analysis">
>
> - If Propane mole % is not measured for one out of 5 days, and there are four records with non-null mole % values and one record with null as mole %, the record with null value is considered to have 0% for propane for average calculation.
> - If Decane mole % was not measured for any of the five days and all five records have null for Decane mole %, then the report will display blank for Decane mole %.
>
> </div>
>
> </div>

If the weight value per the weighted averaging method is null or 0 for all retrieved records, then the simple average is reported instead.

> <div class="example">
>
> <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" style="color: #525f39;" data-mc-targets="Example-Average Analysis 2">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>
>
> <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Average Analysis 2">
>
> If the Rel. Density field on the System Rollup Configuration form is set to “Time Weighted, Linear,” but the flow time on the retrieved records are null, Absolute Density, Relative Density, and Stock Tank Density values will be simple-averaged, instead of weight-averaged.
>
> The following applies to the meter version of the report only:
>
> - Weighted averages for various analysis properties such as Absolute Density, Relative Density, Molar Mass, Volume Ratio, Sediment and Water %,  Shrink Factor, etc. are calculated and displayed on the right side of the report.
> - The averaging method for Absolute Density, Relative Density, and Stock Tank Density will depend on the Rel. Density field value on the System Rollup Configuration form (Admin \> System Options \> Rollup Configuration \> Gas Avg.). The averaging method for Molar Mass, Volume Ratio, S&W %, Shrinkage Factor, and Stock Tank S&W % will depend on the Analysis field value.
> - For the Cn+ Fraction column of the Property table, the weighted averages will not be an accurate representation of the data if the retrieved records have mixed Cn+ Fractions, e.g. some records with C6+ and others with C7+.
>
> </div>
>
> </div>

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Average Location Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Average Location Analysis</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Average Location Analysis">

Displays a weighted average of location analysis data for a selected time frame, calculated by product or total fluid.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Raw Data Count at the top right corner of the report indicates the number of final form daily records that were retrieved as the basis of average calculation according to the selected meter or location, time frame, and product. This report is available as a standard report for FLOWCAL 8.10.50.4 and 8.11.35, or above.

For component mole %, mass %, and liquid volume % average calculation, if a field is null for one or more records, but not all records, the value for the record is considered to be 0, not null. However, if a field is null for all records used for calculation, the average is null and is displayed as blank.

> <div class="example">
>
> <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" style="color: #525f39;" data-mc-targets="Example-Average Loc Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>
>
> <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Average Loc Analysis">
>
> - If Propane mole % is not measured for one out of 5 days, and there are four records with non-null mole % values and one record with null as mole %, the record with null value is considered to have 0% for propane for average calculation.
> - If Decane mole % was not measured for any of the five days and all five records have null for Decane mole %, then the report will display blank for Decane mole %.
>
> </div>
>
> </div>

If the weight value per the weighted averaging method is null or 0 for all retrieved records, then the simple average is reported instead.

> <div class="exampleShrink">
>
> <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" style="color: #525f39;" data-mc-targets="Example-Average Loc Analysis 2">

>

>
> The following applies to the meter version of the report only:
>
> - Weighted averages for various analysis properties such as Absolute Density, Relative Density, Molar Mass, Volume Ratio, Sediment and Water %, Shrink Factor, etc. are calculated and displayed on the right side of the report.
> - The averaging method for Absolute Density, Relative Density, and Stock Tank Density will depend on the Rel. Density field value on the System Rollup Configuration form (Admin \> System Options \> Rollup Configuration \> Gas Avg.). The averaging method for Molar Mass, Volume Ratio, S&W %, Shrinkage Factor, and Stock Tank S&W % will depend on the Analysis field value.
> - For the Cn+ Fraction column of the Property table, the weighted averages will not be an accurate representation of the data if the retrieved records have mixed Cn+ Fractions, e.g. some records with C6+ and others with C7+.
>

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Balance Detail (Full)">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Balance Detail (Full)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Balance Detail (Full)">

Displays gas volume and energy for members of a balance location, grouped by meter direction, meter class, or both. Also displays tickets associated with the balance location according to the ticket direction and ticket class, grouped into ticket types.

Meter volume and energy displayed are for the meter’s full gas month. If the meter is part of the balance location hierarchy only for a part of the reported month, the report displays the full-month quantity. For accurate accounting with regards to the time of relationship, use the Balance Detail (Calc) report.

- **Meter Direction Not Set** - Members with no direction set are displayed in a separate group with the label \<Meter Direction Not Set\>.
- **Inventory Data** - If an inventory location such as a gas inventory, a tank, or a cavern is included in the balance location, any ticket or meter data associated with the inventory does not appear under their directions. Instead, change in the inventory amount held over the reported month in the inventory itself is displayed in a group labeled Change in Inventory.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> At a minimum, the Subtotal By Meter Direction option (Admin \> FLOWCAL Options \> FLOWCAL Configuration) needs to be checked when rolling up balance locations for the report to display the subtotal values associated with each meter direction. If both Subtotal By options are disabled, the subtotal values will not be calculated by the location rollups and the report will not report any subtotal values.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Names: 

- Balance Detail (Full) - By Direction
- Balance Detail (Full) - By Class

</div>

This report displays component values for each meter and ticket in a balance location, grouped by direction, or class and direction. All ticket types are included. Users must specify if they want components displayed as C5+, C6+, or C10. Users can display Component Volume, Component Mass or Component Net Allowable.

Meter volume and energy displayed are for the meter’s full gas month. If the meter is part of the balance location hierarchy only for a part of the reported month, the report displays the full-month quantity.

- **Meter Direction Not Set** - Members with no direction set display at the end of the report with the label \<Meter Direction Not Set\>.
- **Inventory Data** - If an inventory location such as a gas inventory, a tank, or a cavern is included in the balance location, any ticket or meter data associated with the inventory does not appear under their directions. Instead, change in the inventory amount held over the reported month in the inventory itself is displayed in a group labeled Change in Inventory.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> At a minimum, the Subtotal By Meter Direction option (Settings Manager \> Application \> FLOWCAL Configuration) needs to be checked when rolling up balance locations for the report to display the subtotal values associated with each meter direction. If both Subtotal By options are disabled, the subtotal values will not be calculated by the location rollups and the report will not report any subtotal values.

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Component Ticket Statement">

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Component Ticket Statement</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Component Ticket Statement">

This report displays component data for tickets of all ticket types in a location for a given time frame. Tickets are sorted by effective date and ticket number. At the end of all tickets, the totals of quantities for all movement tickets are calculated and displayed.

Users must select whether they want to see components reported to C5+, C6+, or C10 for the report to run. Users must also select if they want to see liquid volume, mass or net allowable components. The report can be run for measured or standard conditions and by product or total fluid.

If displayed tickets have sediment and water data, the report will display gross standard volume, sediment and water percentage, and sediment and water volume.

If displayed tickets do not have any sediment and water percentage or sediment and water volume, the report will display additional component quantities such as summed volume and total net allowable.

The units displayed for measured conditions are based on the units on the reference meter. The units displayed for standard conditions are based on the units on the system that the location belongs to.

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Edit Differences">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Edit Differences</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Edit Differences">

For gas meters, the report displays original volume and energy, current volume and energy, and the difference amount and percent difference for each meter. For liquid meters, the report displays GSV, NSV, and mass amounts from the revision 0 and the most recent revision, the different amount and percent difference for each selected meter.

The difference amount is calculated as:

Current Amount – Original Amount

The percent difference is calculated as:

(Difference Amount / Original Amount) \* 100

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="EFM Data Reconciliation">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> EFM Data Reconciliation</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="EFM Data Reconciliation">

The purpose of this report is to show changes in gas volume values due to edits. The report compares original volume to current volume and displays meters for which the difference between the original and current volumes exceeds the Max Edit Difference specified by the user.

The Max Edit Difference value can be specified either as unit difference or percent difference. To indicate a percent difference, enter a % sign at the end of the value in the field.

- **EFM Volume** - The original (revision 0) volume.

- **Adjusted Volume** - The current volume on the meter as it appears within the Volume Editor.

- **Volume Diff** -
  - For orifice meters, in order to only see volumes due to edits besides GQ apply, the effects of relative density changes resulting from a source apply are backed out. The Volume Diff value displayed on the report is calculated as the difference between the original volume and the volume that is calculated after backing out the specific gravity. The calculation for the volume used in the comparison to the original volume is:

    Current Volume \*<span style="font-family: 'Symbol'"> Ö</span>(current relative density/original relative density)

  - For all other meter types, this value is calculated as the difference between the Adjusted Volume and EFM Volume values.

- **Volume % Diff** - Calculated as:

  (Volume Diff / EFM Volume) \* 100



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 17;height: 17;" /> Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor: 

- Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Name: EFM Data Reconciliation

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> View Sample Report</a>

</div>

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Liquid Balance Detail">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Liquid Balance Detail</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Liquid Balance Detail">

This report displays liquid volumes and mass for each meter in a location, grouped by meter direction. All ticket types are included.

Meter volume and energy displayed are for the meter’s full gas month. If the meter is part of the balance location hierarchy only for a part of the reported month, the report displays the full-month quantity.

- **Meter Direction Not Set** - Members with no direction set display at the end of the report with the label \<Meter Direction Not Set\>.
- **Inventory Data** - If an inventory location such as a gas inventory, a tank, or a cavern is included in the balance location, any ticket or meter data associated with the inventory does not appear under their directions. Instead, change in the inventory amount held over the reported month in the inventory itself is displayed in a group labeled Change in Inventory.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> At a minimum, the Subtotal By Meter Direction option (Admin \> FLOWCAL Options \> FLOWCAL Configuration) needs to be checked when rolling up balance locations for the report to display the subtotal values associated with each meter direction. If both Subtotal By options are disabled, the subtotal values will not be calculated by the location rollups and the report will not report any subtotal values.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Names:

- Liquid Balance Detail - By Direction
- Liquid Balance Detail - By Class



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> View Sample Reports:

- <a href="../../../Resources/PDFs/Report%20Examples/Liquid%20Balance%20Detail%20-%20By%20Direction.pdf" target="_blank">Liquid Balance Detail - By Direction</a>
- <a href="../../../Resources/PDFs/Report%20Examples/Liquid%20Balance%20Detail%20-%20By%20Class.pdf" target="_blank">Liquid Balance Detail - By Class</a>

</div>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Location Daily Comparison">

Displays a daily volume and energy total, as well as the amount difference and percent difference for a segment or a balance location that contains two station location members. This report is designed to work for a location with two station members only. If the location contains multiple levels of locations, the report will drill down and find member station locations. If there are multiple station locations, the report will display the first two that it encounters.

The percent difference is calculated as (Difference/Receipts \* 100). This value displays to one decimal place.

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Meter Batch Ticket">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Meter Batch Ticket</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Meter Batch Ticket">

Provides a summary of all batch tickets within a given date range. Each batch will be displayed on a different page.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> When scheduling this report (Reports \> Report Scheduler \> Scheduler), the functionality to display internal notes is not available. The value for Show Internal Notes parameter is currently always set to No when using the scheduler even when the user selects Yes.

The Meter Batch Ticket and Summary reports display the density values by checking for HC Properties associated with the meter or the Meter's system.

If the Alt. Meter Number is set on the General tab of the Meter Editor and the Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name option is enabled on the Reports tab, the alternate meter number is displayed in place of the meter name.

Component data is displayed only for batches with Table E, COSTALD, or Modified TP-2 products.

The Exception section displays any exceptions 30009-30040 that are generated on the batch, based on the Product Specification criteria set on the Product Editor Validations tab. On the Meter Editor Reports tab, the Show Off Spec on Batch Ticket option needs to be set to “Yes” for this section to be enabled.

When this report is run for a meter that is set up as a BLM property, the report will display the FMP number, lease number, CA number, and PA number.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 17;height: 17;" /> Available Configuration Options in the Meter Editor: 

- Print Customer Name
- Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name
- Print Measurement Area
- Show Off Spec on Batch Ticket



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 17;height: 17;" /> Available Configuration Options in the Product Editor: 

- Show Uncorrected Density

- Show Observed Density

- Show Density Meter Factor

- Show Alkenes

- Show Neo-Pentane

- Show: Use Meter’s Calc. Method \| Volume \| Mass \| Volume and Mass

  Display of density, temperature, pressure, and equilibrium vapor pressure in observed and meter conditions are determined based on the batch’s product table.

  Specifications on the Validations and Discrimination tabs of the Product Editor are fully utilized by this report.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Name: Meter Batch Ticket



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> <a href="../../../Resources/PDFs/Report%20Examples/Meter%20Batch%20Ticket.pdf" target="_blank">View Sample Report</a>

</div>

#### <span id="MeterSampleAnalysis"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Meter Sample and Analysis">

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> This report displays data required by BLM under 43 CFR §§ 3175.113 and 3175.120.

If the meter is designated as a BLM property:

- BLM identification field values are displayed in the top right section of the report.
- For gas meters, the BLM Validation section displays a meter’s Heating Value Variability and Heating Value Uncertainty for its FMP Tier, its Measured Heating Value, and its C6+ split. For more details on calculation of heating value uncertainty and variability, see Heating Value Uncertainty.

Analysis data displayed in this report, including in the Sample and Analysis boxes at the top of the report, is edited in the GQ and LQ Source Analysis Editor (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Gas Quality or Liquid Quality \> Source Analysis tab \> Source Analysis Editor \> Sample tab), and applied to an assigned meter during analysis apply.

The Exception section displays exceptions 30009-30040, based on the Product Specification criteria set on the Product Editor Validations tab. On the Meter Editor Reports tab, the Show Off Spec on Batch Ticket option needs to be set to “Yes” for this section to be enabled.

When scheduling this report (Reports \> Report Scheduler \> Scheduler), the functionality to display internal notes is not available. The value for Show Internal Notes parameter is currently always set to No when using the scheduler even when the user selects Yes.

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Plate Change Notification">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Plate Change Notification</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Plate Change Notification">

Displays orifice meters operating at a low differential pressure and with plate that might be too large. Only meters with a monthly average differential pressure less than 10 and a plate diameter of at least 0.5 will be displayed.

- **Avg DP:** Average differential pressure from the monthly final form meter table
- **DP Range:** High differential pressure transducer limit
- **Pressure:** Average static pressure for gas meters and average meter static pressure from the monthly final form meter table
- **Plate Size:** Current plate (orifice) diameter as of the end of the selected measurement month
- **Tube Size:** Current tube (pipe) diameter as of the end of the selected measurement month
- **Beta Ratio:** Beta ratio is calculated as plate size / tube size.
- **Volume for Month:** Monthly total of volume for gas meters and gross standard volume for liquid meters
- **Flow Time %:** Monthly total actual flow time as % of the complete month flow time



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 17;height: 17;" /> Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor: 

- Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Name: Plate Change Notification

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Significant Flow Change">

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Significant Flow Change</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Significant Flow Change">

Compares volume and energy values from the selected month to those of the previous month, and displays meters for which the change in volume or energy exceeds the value in the Max Monthly Change field specified by the user. The Max Monthly Change value can be specified either as unit difference or percent difference. To indicate a percent difference, enter a % sign at the end of the value in the field. The percent difference is always displayed with two decimal places. It uses the selected month as the denominator. The Max Monthly Change can be the difference (e.g., 20.0) or the percent difference (e.g., 2.0%)



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 17;height: 17;" /> Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor: 

- Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Station Location Verification (Gas)">

Compares the daily or monthly totals for each station location member of a list or location to the sums of all meter and/or ticket member data, displaying any discrepancies. The comparison is performed on volume, energy, and mass (for gas), or GSV, NSV, mass, and summed volume (for liquids). The report assumes that there are no date/time splits on the station location and that multipliers of 1 are specified for all meter members.

Gauge Deliveries accounts for changes in tank inventory where a gauge shows a decrease in volume that is not accounted for by a meter or ticket delivery.

#### <span id="TicketDetail"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Ticket Detail">

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Ticket Detail</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ticket Detail">

This report displays detailed ticket data, including measurement data, accounting information, and component quantities, for all applicable ticket types in the selected location for a given time frame. Each ticket will be displayed on a different page. When this report is run for a ticket attached to a location or a tank that is set up as a BLM property, the report will display the FMP number, lease number, CA number, and PA number.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Name: Ticket Detail

#### <span id="TicketDetailAllowables"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Ticket Detail Allowables">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Ticket Detail Allowables</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ticket Detail Allowables">

This report displays detailed ticket data, including measurement data, accounting information, and net allowable quantities, for all applicable ticket types in the selected location for a given time frame. Each ticket will be displayed on a different page. When this report is run for a ticket attached to a location or a tank that is set up as a BLM property, the report will display the FMP number, lease number, CA number, and PA number. When the report is run for a ticket using US Customary units, the component volumes and net allowables values are reported in gallons, regardless of the component volume units on the ticket.

The Component section contains:

- All component data available for the ticket, up to the highest component.
- Alkenes and neopentane if the "Show Alkenes" and "Show Neo-Pentane" options are enabled for the ticket.
- Component mass data for meter tickets using the mass-based calculation method. In this case, the report displays density values for each component pulled from the HC Properties data.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> To determine the Density values on the report, FLOWCAL first looks at the source to determine which HC properties values to display, then the system-level HC properties.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Name: Ticket Detail Allowables



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> View Sample Report: <a href="../../../Resources/PDFs/Report%20Examples/Ticket%20Detail%20Allowables.pdf" target="_blank">Ticket Detail Allowables - Location</a>

</div>

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Ticket Volume Statement">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Ticket Volume Statement</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ticket Volume Statement">

This report displays flow data for tickets of all ticket types in a location for a given time frame. Tickets are sorted by effective date and ticket number. At the end of all tickets, the totals of quantities for all movement tickets are calculated and displayed.

If displayed tickets have sediment and water data, the report will display gross standard volume, sediment and water percentage, and sediment and water volume.

If displayed tickets do not have any sediment and water percentage or sediment and water volume, the report will display additional component quantities such as summed volume and total net allowable.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="Icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> Schedule Editor Group Name:

- Ticket Volume Statement (By Product)
- Ticket Volume Statement (By Total Fluid)

#### <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerexception MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_exception MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Volume Statement">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />

<img src="data:image/bmp;base64," class="Icon" /> Volume Statement</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Volume Statement">

The Volume Statements can be found on the report menu by selecting the Volume Statement option. These reports display daily or hourly flow data for gas or liquid meters. The report includes meter configuration and analysis data for the last flow record. Each daily (or hourly) value is displayed on the report along with any prior period adjustments that may have occurred during the month.

##### Edit Reasons

Edit reasons can be displayed for a meter by selecting the Print Edit Reasons option on the Reports tab of the Meter Editor. The edit reasons will always start on the second page of the daily report. The hourly report displays the edit reasons at the bottom of the page.

##### PPA Edit

PPA edits will display for every meter with PPAs for the measurement month. The PPA edit will begin after the meter edit reasons if those are set to print in the Meter Editor. If the edit reasons do not display, the PPA edits will display on page 2.

##### PPA Accounted for During the Month

The PPA Accounted for section displays only if the applicable flags are setup in System Configurations on the PPA and Approvals tab. The Set Accounting Month To options needs to be checked for the Accounted for information to display on the GVS. This section displays after the PPA Edits.

This accounted for section has the option to include the accounted for totals or not. If the user wants to see the totals, the Show Total on GVS report option in System Configuration must be checked.

##### Additional Report Behavior

When running the report for liquid and by product, each product is displayed on a different page.

- The composition section of the Volume Statement (Liquid) reports will be suppressed if the total component liquid volume percent and total mass percent are both 0 or null.
- Volume Statement (Liquid) reports will not display pulses for meters that have the "Calculate from Pulses" option in Meter Characteristics set to "No".
- Volume Statement (Liquid) reports will display sediment and water percentage and volume only for meters that have non-zero sediment and water.
- When the selected month has PPA edits, the PPA Adjustments and Edit Reasons section will appear on the second page.
- When the Accounting Month for PPAs setting is enabled, the PPAs Accounted For During the Month section will display on the second page. In addition to listing the PPAs accounted for during the month, their totals will be calculated and displayed if the Show Total On GVS Report option is enabled.
